title: Machine learning model with post-hoc SHAP interpretation based on perioperative clinical and imaging parameters for prediction of 1-year radiographic recurrence after hallux valgus
summary: A machine-learning model trained on 389 cases and temporally validated in 208 cases predicts one-year radiographic recurrence after hallux-valgus surgery; the result is prognostic performance, not causal treatment guidance.
ai_technology: Machine-learning prediction of one-year radiographic recurrence
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: A machine-learning model trained on 389 cases and temporally validated in 208 cases predicts one-year radiographic recurrence after hallux-valgus surgery; the result is prognostic performance, not causal treatment guidance.
evidence.unknown: A later temporal holdout supports internal prognostic validation; single-center data and event count limit transportability; no causal or clinical-benefit claim is made.
evidence.ai_role: SVM/model-based prediction integrates perioperative clinical and imaging parameters; SHAP interprets feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
